clue.text: Party at Burlington House for a star group

parts.note: LIB is short for the Liberal party
Burlington House in London is home of the Royal Academy, abbreviated RA

explanation.surface: An invitation to a party at a London gallery held for a group of celebrities.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Star group' looks like celebrities but means a constellation. Burlington House, on Piccadilly in London, houses the Royal Academy of Arts.
explanation.definitionFit: Libra is one of the zodiac constellations, a named cluster of stars in the sky.

clue.text: I object to cane-swishing as a threat

parts.note: the pronoun I used as a grammatical object is me

indicators.note: a cane being swished about suggests its letters being thrown around into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone protests that waving a cane about is intimidating behaviour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swishing' rearranges CANE into ACE, placed after ME.
explanation.definitionFit: A menace is a danger or source of intimidation, much the same as a threat.

clue.text: In fine form it is immeasurable

indicators.note: putting the letters into another form signals that they are to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Something in excellent condition is beyond all measuring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Form' rearranges the letters of IN FINE plus IT into the answer; 'In fine form' reads as a phrase meaning in good shape.
explanation.definitionFit: Something without limits or end cannot be measured.

clue.text: A hellish prospect of staying out

indicators.note: out here means the letters are out of place, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: The thought of having to stay put strikes someone as a grim, hellish prospect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Out' rearranges STAYING. 'A' and 'prospect of' only join the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Stygian comes from the Styx, the river of the underworld in Greek myth, so it means infernal or gloomily dark.

clue.text: Inquisitive person with all the answers

definitions.text: Inquisitive person with all the answers

parts.words: Inquisitive person with all the answers
parts.note: reads like a nosy know-all, but describes the host of a quiz, who asks everything and holds the answer sheet

explanation.surface: A nosy busybody who seems to know everything.
explanation.definitionFit: The host of a quiz night poses the questions and holds every correct reply.

clue.text: Recopying can be so feverish

indicators.note: the letters of the word can be made into something else, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Copying out work again can bring on a fever.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Can be' signals that RECOPYING is rearranged; 'so' links.
explanation.definitionFit: Pyrogenic means producing heat or fever, hence feverish.

clue.text: Breathe in a way to avoid winter exposure

indicators.note: put another way, the letters are given a new order

explanation.surface: Advice to inhale in a particular manner to keep out the winter cold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In a way' looks like the indicator, but IN is needed for the anagram: BREATHE IN rearranged, signalled by 'a way'.
explanation.definitionFit: Animals that sleep through the cold months shelter themselves from the winter weather.

clue.text: Sustains youngsters going round the bend

indicators.note: the youngsters going round something means their word encloses it

parts.note: young males are boys
a U-bend is a bend shaped like the letter U

explanation.surface: A carer keeps young lads going as they take a corner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Going round' puts BOYS round U.
explanation.definitionFit: To buoy is to keep afloat or keep up someone's spirits, which is to hold them up.

clue.text: Cut up rough

definitions.meaning: short, broken waves on choppy water

explanation.definitionFit: To chop food is to cut it into pieces, and chop is also the term for broken, choppy water on the sea.

clue.text: Sounds like sovereign bird's dying!

indicators.note: the clue says the result is heard like the words that follow

parts.note: a sovereign is a king and the bird is a crow, so a monarch crow said aloud

explanation.surface: An exclamation about the noises made by a royal bird at its death.
explanation.walkthrough: CROW KING said aloud sounds like the answer; the bird and the sovereign come in the reverse order.
explanation.definitionFit: To croak is a slang way of saying to die, so croaking means on the point of death.

clue.text: Aromatic plant Sophy's ordered

indicators.note: Sophy's letters are ordered, put into a fresh arrangement

parts.note: the name together with its S, taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: Sophy has placed an order for a fragrant herb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ordered' rearranges the six letters of SOPHYS, the S of the possessive included.
explanation.definitionFit: Hyssop is a scented herb of the mint family, used in cooking and medicine.

clue.text: Son of Jacob from a little village

indicators.note: the answer is taken from the words that follow, sitting inside them

explanation.surface: A biblical figure who hailed from a small village.
explanation.walkthrough: 'From' takes the answer out of littLE VIllage.
explanation.definitionFit: Levi was the third son of Jacob and Leah and founder of the priestly tribe in the Bible.

clue.text: A past president gets up and tells all

parts.note: PP is the abbreviation for past president
to get up from bed is to rise

explanation.surface: A former head of state rises to give a full account.
explanation.walkthrough: PP stands for past president, as on lists of society officers.
explanation.definitionFit: To apprise someone is to inform them, letting them know everything.

clue.text: Foreshadowed the last of the wine

parts.note: port is a fortified wine
read as the moment something reaches its end, so it has ended

explanation.surface: An omen seen in the dregs of a bottle.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'the last of the wine' as PORT that has ENDED.
explanation.definitionFit: To portend is to give a warning sign of what is coming, which is to presage it.

clue.text: Found on the range, after the game?

definitions.meaning: a pan for cooking eggs, used on a kitchen stove
someone who hunts animals or birds illegally

explanation.surface: Something seen on the hills or a cooking range once the match is over.
explanation.walkthrough: A range is a kitchen cooker; 'game' looks like a match but means birds and animals hunted.
explanation.definitionFit: An egg pan sits on a stove, and an illegal hunter goes after deer or pheasants.

clue.text: Transport vehicle with one gear slipping

parts.note: a car is a vehicle

indicators.note: a gear slipping goes out of place, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A vehicle whose gearbox keeps slipping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Slipping' rearranges I plus GEAR into RIAGE, after CAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Carriage is the conveying of goods from place to place, a kind of shipping.

clue.text: Extreme feature of wild elation

indicators.note: wild letters run free and land in a new order

explanation.surface: Ecstatic joy, wild in the extreme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wild' rearranges ELATION. A nail on a toe sits at the body's extremity.
explanation.definitionFit: A nail on the foot sits at a body extremity, so it is a part found at the end of a limb.

clue.text: Win easily though not in form

parts.note: not in is out
a form is a school class

explanation.surface: A competitor wins comfortably despite being out of form.
explanation.walkthrough: In British schools a form is a class of pupils.
explanation.definitionFit: To be far superior to a rival is to beat them with ease.

clue.text: Hold charge for second haul

parts.note: towage is the act of towing, a haul

explanation.surface: A fee to be held for a second shipment.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition reads as a fee for holding things, the charge made for storage.
explanation.definitionFit: Stowage is both storage space and the payment made for storing goods.

clue.text: Brilliant role average in the beginning

indicators.note: one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: a beginning is a start
par is the average or normal standard

explanation.surface: Someone's dazzling performance began as merely average.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' puts PAR inside START, after its first four letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A leading part in a play goes to the top performer, the lead role.

clue.text: Movement in Laos, too

indicators.note: a movement among the letters of the country shifts them into a new order

explanation.surface: A political movement in the Asian country of Laos as well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Movement in' rearranges LAOS.
explanation.definitionFit: Also and too both mean in addition.

clue.text: Pack it in, thanks to parliamentarian support

parts.note: ta is informal British for thanks
MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: Someone told to give up, thanks to backing from their MP.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pack it in' sounds like an order to quit but means press down; 'to' and 'support' join the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: To tamp is to press material down firmly, as when filling a pipe.

clue.text: See 5
Sound as a bell

parts.note: reads as the idiom for perfectly healthy, but means the tolling noise of a bell

explanation.surface: Someone declared in perfect health.
explanation.definitionFit: A knell is the slow toll of a bell, rung for a death or funeral.

clue.text: Type of rock different singers don't get right

indicators.note: the singers are made different, rearranged

explanation.surface: Some vocalists struggle with a kind of rock music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Don't get right' drops R from SINGERS; 'different' rearranges what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: Gneiss is a banded metamorphic rock.

clue.text: English town Berliners would welcome

definitions.meaning: a town on Tyneside in north-east England
the end of the Berlin Wall, welcomed in 1989

explanation.surface: A town in England that people in Berlin would be pleased to see.
explanation.walkthrough: Wallsend is on the Tyne near Newcastle, where Hadrian's Wall ends; read as WALL'S END it is the fall of the Berlin Wall.
explanation.definitionFit: The town is named for the eastern end of Hadrian's Wall, and Berliners cheered the end of their own wall.

clue.text: Work unit points out it's material

indicators.note: the points are on the outside of the unit

parts.note: S and E are compass points
the erg is a unit of work in physics

explanation.surface: A unit at work points out that it is made of fabric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Out' puts the compass points S and E outside ERG.
explanation.definitionFit: Serge is a hard-wearing twilled fabric used for suits and uniforms.

clue.text: Yellow and white containers

parts.note: reads like coloured boxes, but describes what holds yolk and albumen

explanation.surface: Boxes painted in yellow and white.
explanation.definitionFit: The shell of a hen's egg encloses the yolk and the white.
